title: Although, Though, Despite and In Spite Of
summary: Express an unexpected contrast using although, though, even though, despite and in spite of. Choose a complete clause or a noun/-ing phrase correctly, and distinguish concession from a reason introduced by because.
learningObjectives: Connect an unexpected result to a contrasting fact with although, though or even though followed by a full clause.
Use despite and in spite of with a noun phrase, a pronoun or an -ing form rather than a bare finite clause.
Use despite the fact that and in spite of the fact that when a full clause must follow these prepositions.
Use sentence-final though in conversation and distinguish contrasting facts from causes expressed with because or because of.

explanation.heading: Although and though link contrasting facts
explanation.body: Use although or though before a clause containing a subject and a verb. The clause introduces a fact that makes the main result unexpected. The contrast can come before or after the main clause. When it comes first, a comma normally separates the clauses. These connectors do not give a reason; they signal that the result happened despite an obstacle or expectation.
explanation.example: Although the hall was almost empty, the performers gave a lively show.

explanation.heading: Despite and in spite of take phrases, not bare clauses
explanation.body: Use despite or in spite of before a noun phrase, a pronoun such as that, or an -ing form. Both mean that something happened contrary to what the circumstances suggested. Despite does not take of, whereas in spite of must include of. Do not place a normal subject + finite verb directly after either expression.
explanation.example: In spite of losing their luggage, the travellers remained cheerful.

explanation.heading: The fact that makes a full clause possible
explanation.body: When you want a complete subject-and-verb clause after despite or in spite of, add the fact that: despite the fact that + clause. This structure is grammatically correct but can be wordier than although + clause. Choose the shorter option when the extra emphasis is not needed.
explanation.example: Despite the fact that the lift was broken, the exhibition remained accessible.

explanation.heading: Even though strengthens a real contrast
explanation.body: Even though works like although but often makes the surprising contrast stronger. It introduces a fact known to be true, not just a possible future condition. Use even though + subject + verb; even on its own cannot replace this connector before a full clause.
explanation.example: Even though the route was clearly marked, several runners missed the turning.

explanation.heading: Though in conversation, and concession versus cause
explanation.body: Though is common in conversation and can appear at the end of a separate sentence to mean something like however. Although cannot normally occupy that final position. Compare concession with reason: although the ticket was expensive tells us an unexpected contrast, while because the ticket was expensive supplies a reason for a decision. With nouns, because of introduces a cause, not a concession.
explanation.example: The café was noisy. The coffee was excellent, though.

comparisons.title: Full clause versus noun or -ing phrase

left.label: Although + clause
left.example: Although the street was flooded, the buses kept running.
left.note: The connector is followed by the subject the street and the finite verb was.

right.label: Despite + noun
right.example: Despite the flooding, the buses kept running.
right.note: Despite takes the noun phrase the flooding; no of is added.

comparisons.title: A contrasting fact versus a reason

left.label: Concession
left.example: We stayed outside despite the wind.
left.note: The wind might have made us go indoors, but it did not.

right.label: Cause
right.example: We went indoors because of the wind.
right.note: The wind explains why we decided to go inside.

comparisons.title: Emphasis at the beginning versus a conversational afterthought

left.label: Even though + clause
left.example: Even though the film was long, I watched it twice.
left.note: The unexpected contrast is emphasized before the main message.

right.label: Final though
right.example: The film was long. I enjoyed it, though.
right.note: The second sentence adds a contrasting comment in conversational style.

examples.sentence: Although the deadline was tight, we checked every figure before submitting the report.
examples.note: Although introduces a complete contrasting clause about the deadline.

examples.sentence: Despite a minor delay, the train reached its destination before dark.
examples.note: Despite takes the noun phrase a minor delay.

examples.sentence: The musicians continued playing in spite of feeling exhausted.
examples.note: In spite of is followed by an -ing phrase.

examples.sentence: Even though he had rehearsed carefully, Daniel forgot the opening line.
examples.note: Even though emphasizes a surprising result despite a known preparation.

examples.sentence: The apartment is small. It gets plenty of sunlight, though.
examples.note: Sentence-final though gives an informal contrasting afterthought.

examples.sentence: Despite the fact that the shop was closing, the assistant helped the last customer.
examples.note: The fact that permits a subject-and-verb clause after despite.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Despite of the rain, the picnic continued.
commonMistakes.correct: Despite the rain, the picnic continued.
commonMistakes.why: Despite does not include of; in spite of is the separate three-word expression.

commonMistakes.incorrect: In spite of the road was narrow, the driver stayed calm.
commonMistakes.correct: Although the road was narrow, the driver stayed calm.
commonMistakes.why: A subject-and-verb clause can follow although, but not in spite of without the fact that.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Even the manager was tired, she stayed to help.
commonMistakes.correct: Even though the manager was tired, she stayed to help.
commonMistakes.why: Even alone cannot introduce a full concessive clause; use even though.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The laptop was old. It still worked well, although.
commonMistakes.correct: The laptop was old. It still worked well, though.
commonMistakes.why: In conversational English, though can stand at the end of a contrasting sentence; although normally cannot.

studyTips: Before choosing a connector, underline the words immediately after it: subject + verb needs although/though/even though, while noun or -ing suits despite/in spite of.
Write one factual contrast in two ways, replacing an although-clause with a despite + noun or -ing phrase without changing its meaning.
Check whether a second idea is surprising or causal; choose although/despite for contrast and because/because of for a reason.

exercises.prompt: The doors were difficult to open, but everyone entered the hall. Choose the sentence with a correct full-clause connector.
choices: Despite the doors were heavy, everyone entered.
Although the doors were heavy, everyone entered.
In spite of the doors were heavy, everyone entered.
exercises.feedback: Although takes the full clause the doors were heavy; despite and in spite of cannot directly take it.

exercises.prompt: The path was muddy, but the group finished its walk. Which sentence correctly uses a preposition followed by a noun?
choices: Despite the mud, the group finished its walk.
Despite of the mud, the group finished its walk.
Although the mud, the group finished its walk.
exercises.feedback: Despite is followed directly by the noun phrase the mud, without of.

exercises.prompt: You know that an employee had little experience, yet she led the project successfully. Which version emphasizes this surprising contrast?
choices: Even she had little experience, she led the project successfully.
Because she had little experience, she led the project successfully.
Even though she had little experience, she led the project successfully.
exercises.feedback: Even though links a real situation with a contrary-to-expectation outcome.

exercises.prompt: A friend says the accommodation was expensive and then adds a positive comment informally. Choose the natural ending.
choices: The view was beautiful, although.
The view was beautiful, despite.
The view was beautiful, though.
exercises.feedback: Final though adds an informal contrasting afterthought; although and despite cannot be used that way.

exercises.prompt: ___ the kitchen was small, the restaurant served fifty guests comfortably. (one-word connector before a complete clause)
acceptedAnswers: Although
Though
exercises.feedback: Although or though correctly introduces the full clause the kitchen was small.

exercises.prompt: ___ the broken heating, the office remained open. (use the one-word preposition meaning in spite of)
acceptedAnswers: Despite
exercises.feedback: Despite takes the noun phrase the broken heating directly; it never needs of.

exercises.prompt: The team delivered on time in ___ of several unexpected setbacks. (complete the fixed prepositional expression)
acceptedAnswers: spite
exercises.feedback: In spite of + noun phrase expresses a contrast despite setbacks.

exercises.prompt: The event was successful despite the ___ that very few tickets had been sold. (complete the expression allowing a full clause)
acceptedAnswers: fact
exercises.feedback: Despite the fact that makes it grammatical to follow despite with a complete clause.

exercises.prompt: Correct the connector only: Despite of the noise, I completed my assignment.
acceptedAnswers: Despite the noise, I completed my assignment.
exercises.feedback: Despite never takes of. A noun phrase follows it directly.

exercises.prompt: Correct the connector to introduce the existing complete clause: In spite of the tickets were expensive, we attended the concert.
acceptedAnswers: Although the tickets were expensive, we attended the concert.
Though the tickets were expensive, we attended the concert.
exercises.feedback: A complete clause with subject the tickets and verb were requires although or though rather than in spite of alone.

exercises.prompt: Correct the clause opener, keeping the known fact and outcome: Even the road was closed, the delivery arrived on time.
acceptedAnswers: Even though the road was closed, the delivery arrived on time.
exercises.feedback: Even though, not even alone, introduces a full clause stating a fact in contrast with the result.

exercises.prompt: Correct the final connector only: The course was demanding. I learned a lot, although.
acceptedAnswers: The course was demanding. I learned a lot, though.
exercises.feedback: Sentence-final though is natural for an informal contrasting afterthought.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use the given contrasting facts in one sentence: the gallery was crowded; we enjoyed the visit. Begin with "Although the gallery was crowded".
acceptedAnswers: Although the gallery was crowded, we enjoyed the visit.
speakingExercises.feedback: Although is followed by a complete clause and a contrasting main statement.

speakingExercises.prompt: Rewrite this contrast as one sentence using "despite": the wind was strong; the ferry sailed. Begin with "Despite the strong wind".
acceptedAnswers: Despite the strong wind, the ferry sailed.
speakingExercises.feedback: Despite takes the noun phrase the strong wind.

speakingExercises.prompt: Say a sentence using exactly these facts: she felt nervous; she gave a clear presentation. Begin with "In spite of feeling nervous".
acceptedAnswers: In spite of feeling nervous, she gave a clear presentation.
speakingExercises.feedback: An -ing phrase can follow in spite of to express a concession.

speakingExercises.prompt: The roads were icy, but the driver arrived safely. The icy roads are a confirmed fact. Emphasize the contrast in one sentence beginning "Even though the roads were icy".
acceptedAnswers: Even though the roads were icy, the driver arrived safely.
speakingExercises.feedback: Even though emphasizes an outcome that is surprising given a real circumstance.

speakingExercises.prompt: Make two short sentences from these facts: the hotel room was tiny; the bed was comfortable. Put "though" at the end of the second sentence. Begin with "The hotel room".
acceptedAnswers: The hotel room was tiny. The bed was comfortable, though.
speakingExercises.feedback: Though at the end is a natural spoken afterthought expressing contrast.

speakingExercises.prompt: Use the formal pattern "despite the fact that" with these facts: the server was slow; the files were delivered. Begin with "Despite the fact that the server was slow".
acceptedAnswers: Despite the fact that the server was slow, the files were delivered.
speakingExercises.feedback: Despite the fact that can be followed by a complete subject-and-verb clause.

speakingExercises.prompt: Rewrite the reason as a contrast while keeping the same factual result. Original: "We continued hiking because the weather was good." New facts: weather was bad; we continued hiking. Begin with "Although".
acceptedAnswers: Although the weather was bad, we continued hiking.
speakingExercises.feedback: Although introduces a contrasting circumstance, not the cause of the hike.

speakingExercises.prompt: Produce exactly two sentences using the supplied facts. First: the exam was difficult; Ana passed. Begin with "Although". Second: she felt tired; she celebrated. Begin with "Despite feeling tired".
acceptedAnswers: Although the exam was difficult, Ana passed. Despite feeling tired, she celebrated.
speakingExercises.feedback: The first sentence uses a full clause after although; the second uses an -ing phrase after despite.

listeningExercises.audioText: Although the power went out briefly, the visitors completed the museum tour.
listeningExercises.prompt: What did the visitors do despite the problem?
choices: They cancelled the tour.
They completed the tour.
They postponed the tour until Saturday.
listeningExercises.feedback: Although indicates that the power cut did not stop the visitors from completing the tour.

listeningExercises.audioText: Despite a steep hill near the end, the cyclist reached the village on time.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which obstacle failed to prevent the cyclist from arriving on time?
choices: A steep hill.
A flat tyre.
Heavy traffic.
listeningExercises.feedback: Despite introduces the obstacle, a steep hill, that did not prevent an on-time arrival.

listeningExercises.audioText: Even though the team had very little rehearsal time, their performance was excellent.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word connector heard at the very beginning of the sentence.
acceptedAnswers: Even though
listeningExercises.feedback: Even though introduces a confirmed reason for expecting a different result.

listeningExercises.audioText: We waited nearly an hour for our food. The meal was excellent, though.
listeningExercises.prompt: How did the speaker feel about the meal overall?
choices: The meal was disappointing in every way.
The speaker disliked the food but liked the service.
The speaker liked the meal, despite one criticism.
listeningExercises.feedback: The final though adds the positive contrast: the meal was excellent despite the long wait.

listeningExercises.audioText: Our flight left late because of thick fog near the runway.
listeningExercises.prompt: What relationship does the speaker express between the fog and the delay?
choices: The fog caused the delayed departure.
The plane left early despite the fog.
The fog happened after the departure.
listeningExercises.feedback: Because of supplies the cause of the departure delay, rather than an unexpected contrast.

listeningExercises.audioText: In spite of the shop being closed to customers, the staff were preparing online orders inside.
listeningExercises.prompt: Which pair of facts is true?
choices: The lights were on and nobody entered.
The shop was shut, but staff continued preparing orders.
The shop was open and customers were collecting orders.
listeningExercises.feedback: In spite of the closure marks the unexpected continuation of staff activity.

listeningExercises.audioText: The outdoor class continued despite the cold weather and occasional wind.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the one-word preposition heard immediately before "the cold weather".
acceptedAnswers: despite
listeningExercises.feedback: Despite takes the noun phrase the cold weather without of.

listeningExercises.audioText: In spite of the fact that the entrance was blocked, people found another way in.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word prepositional expression at the beginning of the recording, immediately before "the fact that".
acceptedAnswers: in spite of
listeningExercises.feedback: In spite of takes the phrase the fact that before the complete clause the entrance was blocked.
